grammarPoint.title: Collective nouns and agreement
grammarPoint.summary: Learn how collective nouns like 'team' and phrases like 'a number of' and 'the majority' determine singular or plural verb agreement.
grammarPoint.explanation:
Collective nouns refer to a group of people or things as a single unit (e.g., *team*, *family*, *government*). In American English, these nouns usually take a *singular* verb when the group acts as one entity. However, if the members of the group are acting individually, a *plural* verb can be used, though this is less common in American English than British English.

The phrase "*a number of*" always takes a *plural* verb because it emphasizes the individual items or people within the group. For example, "A number of issues *were* discussed."

"*The majority*" can take either a singular or plural verb. When it refers to the group as a single unit, use a *singular* verb. When it refers to the individual members of the group, especially when followed by "of + plural noun," use a *plural* verb. For instance, "The majority *is* against the proposal" (as a unit) versus "The majority of employees *are* happy with the new policy" (individuals).
patterns: A number of + plural noun + plural verb
The majority of + plural noun + plural verb

examples.text: The committee *meets* every Tuesday to review applications.
examples.note: The committee acts as a single unit, so a singular verb is used.

examples.text: The audience *were* all standing and cheering for the band.
examples.note: The audience members are acting individually, so a plural verb is used.

examples.text: A number of new restaurants *have* opened downtown recently.
examples.note: The phrase 'a number of' always takes a plural verb.

examples.text: The majority *is* expected to vote in favor of the new policy.
examples.note: Here, 'the majority' refers to the group as a single entity, taking a singular verb.

examples.text: The majority of students *prefer* online classes this semester.
examples.note: When 'the majority' is followed by 'of + plural noun', it usually takes a plural verb.

commonErrors.wrong: A number of people is waiting outside.
commonErrors.right: A number of people *are* waiting outside.
commonErrors.note: 'A number of' always requires a plural verb.

commonErrors.wrong: The team are celebrating its victory.
commonErrors.note: If the team acts as a unit, use a singular verb and pronoun.

commonErrors.wrong: The majority of the citizens believes in the plan.
commonErrors.right: The majority of the citizens *believe* in the plan.
commonErrors.note: When 'the majority of' refers to individuals, use a plural verb.

exercises.question: The staff ___ decided to implement the new software next month.
exercises.explanation: When 'staff' acts as a single unit making a collective decision, a singular verb ('has') is appropriate.

exercises.question: A number of important details ___ overlooked in the initial report.
exercises.explanation: 'A number of' always takes a plural verb, so 'were' is correct.

exercises.question: The majority of the committee members ___ against the proposal.
exercises.explanation: When 'the majority of' refers to individual members, a plural verb ('are') is used.

exercises.question: The government ___ planning to introduce new environmental regulations.
exercises.explanation: The government is acting as a single unit, so a singular verb ('is') is correct.

exercises.text: The family ___ going on vacation together next week.
exercises.explanation: The family is acting as a single unit, so the singular verb 'is' is correct.

exercises.text: A number of new ideas ___ presented during the brainstorming session.
exercises.explanation: 'A number of' always takes a plural verb, so 'were' is correct.

exercises.text: The majority of the voters ___ still undecided about the upcoming election.
exercises.explanation: When 'the majority of' refers to individual voters, a plural verb ('are') is used.

exercises.explanation: 'A number of' always takes a plural verb, so 'agree' is correct.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: The company are launching its new product line soon.
answers: The company is launching its new product line soon.
exercises.explanation: When 'company' acts as a single unit, it takes a singular verb ('is').

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: The majority of the participants was satisfied with the workshop.
answers: The majority of the participants were satisfied with the workshop.
exercises.explanation: When 'the majority of' refers to individual participants, a plural verb ('were') is used.

exercises.source: Many students have expressed interest in the advanced course.
answers: A number of students have expressed interest in the advanced course.
exercises.explanation: 'A number of' replaces 'many' and correctly takes a plural verb.

exercises.source: Most of the population supports the new environmental initiative.
answers: The majority of the population supports the new environmental initiative.
exercises.explanation: 'The majority of' can be used here, and 'population' as a unit takes a singular verb.
